name: Water pump
what: The water pump circulates coolant through the engine and cooling system.
why: Coolant flow carries heat away from the cylinder block and head to help maintain operating temperature.
where: The pump mounts at the timing-belt end of the B-series engine and is driven by the timing belt.
installationReason: The pump mounts on the timing-belt end of the block. Its pulley is driven by the timing belt; the exact mounting and sealing details vary by B16 version.

guide.overview: The water pump circulates coolant through the block, cylinder head, and radiator circuit.
guide.operation: The timing belt drives the pump impeller. The rotating impeller moves coolant through the engine's water jackets and onward through the cooling system.
guide.construction: This educational model shows a cast pump housing, circular mounting flange, central shaft hub, and pulley face. It is a simplified procedural representation, not factory CAD.
guide.specifications: Pump dimensions, pulley details, gasket specification, fastener torque, and coolant flow data are not asserted. Verify against the exact B16 variant's service information.
guide.inspection: Check the housing for cracks or corrosion, inspect the shaft for play or leakage, and check the sealing surface and gasket. Follow the specified replacement procedure.
guide.failureModes: Bearing wear, seal leakage, corrosion, or impeller damage can reduce coolant circulation and lead to overheating.
